name: Transcribe (Auto-Detect)
description: Use this when: you don't know the document's script type and want automatic routing. Classifies the script type (Typescript / Manuscript / HTR / Paleography) then runs the matching transcription profile — including two-pass review for historical and archaic scripts.

config.prompt:
Transcribe the text visible on this image. The document is typewritten or printed.

Rules:
- Output ONLY the transcription. No headings, preamble, commentary, or summary.
- Preserve original layout, line breaks, and paragraph structure.
- Preserve original spelling, capitalisation, and punctuation exactly as printed.
- Include every visible text element — headers, body, footers, page numbers, marginalia, stamps, annotations.
- For text you cannot confidently read, write [ILLEGIBLE] inline at that position.
- If the image contains no text, output [no text].

Transcribe the handwritten text visible on this image. The document contains modern handwriting (20th–21st century).

Rules:
- Output ONLY the transcription. No headings, preamble, commentary, or summary.
- Preserve original layout, line breaks, and paragraph structure.
- Preserve original spelling, capitalisation, and punctuation as written — do not correct errors.
- Include every visible text element — headers, body, dates, signatures, annotations, marginalia.
- Transcribe signatures as written (the full signed name if legible).
- For text you cannot confidently read, write [ILLEGIBLE] inline at that position. Do not guess.
- Do NOT invent or normalise content. What is on the page is the source of truth.
- If the image contains no legible text, output [no text].

You are performing Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) on a historical document (16th-19th C.). Produce a DRAFT transcription — this is Pass 1 of 2. Favour coverage over perfection; a reviewer will correct errors in Pass 2.

**Before transcribing, note in a single bracketed line:**
[Script: <itálica / cortesana / procesal / redonda / alemana / other>; century: <approx. range>; language: <Spanish/Latin/other>]

Then output ONLY the transcription.

**Rules:**
- Output ONLY the transcription. No headings, preamble, or commentary.
- Preserve original layout, line breaks, and paragraph structure.
- Preserve original spelling, capitalisation, and punctuation exactly. Do NOT modernise, normalise, or correct.
- Archaic letterforms → modern equivalents: long-s → s, thorn → th, yogh → y/g.
- Abbreviations: expand only when unambiguous; expanded letters in [brackets]. When uncertain, transcribe the abbreviation literally. Common 16th-19th C. abbreviations: Vmd (Vuestra Merced), dho/dha (dicho/dicha), q̄ (que), tpo (tiempo), Sr. (Señor), S.M. (Su Majestad).
- Two-tier uncertainty: [UNCERTAIN] for a plausible reading; [ILLEGIBLE] for truly unreadable text.
- Include all visible text: headers, body, marginalia, stamps, signatures.
- Signatures: transcribe as written.
- Crossed-out text: [deleted: <text>].
- Inserted text above the line: include inline at the insertion point.
- Marginalia: include at their position prefixed with [M.N.].
- Rubric/flourish below a signature: [Rúbrica].
- Seals and stamps: [Sello] or [Estampilla].
- No legible text: [sin texto].

You are reviewing a draft HTR transcription against its original manuscript image.

The draft appears in the Context section above. Use the **comparison method** to resolve uncertainties: identify a few clearly legible words, then use their letters as reference standards to measure ambiguous characters elsewhere on the page.

**Common HTR error patterns to check:**

Cursive confusions (all periods):
- rn → m (or vice versa), c → e, u → n, v → u, i → e
- Long-s mistaken for f; t confused with l
- Ligatured pairs (ct, st) read as single letters

16th-17th C. (procesal / cortesana):
- Heavily abbreviated line-endings: check that expansions are plausible
- Baseline-stretched letters and knotty connections hiding word boundaries
- Digit confusions: 1/7, 0/o, 5/6
- Common abbreviated forms: Vmd, dho, dha, q̄, tpo, mrd, qta, Sor

18th-19th C. (itálica):
- Words not uniformly separated (itálica writes fast, spacing irregular)
- Superscript abbreviations: verify the expanded word matches the period
- Names and places: check spelling character-by-character against the image

All scripts:
- Marginalia, stamps, rubrics, or crossed-out text the draft skipped
- Inserted words above the line the draft dropped
- Numbers and dates: verify every digit

**Rules:**
- Output ONLY the corrected transcription. No commentary, diff, or preamble.
- Keep the script identification line from the draft (update if wrong).
- Preserve original orthography. Do NOT modernise.
- If the draft is already correct, return it verbatim.
- Keep conventions: [UNCERTAIN], [ILLEGIBLE], [deleted: ...], [M.N.], [Rúbrica], [Sello].

You are a paleographer producing a DRAFT transcription of a historical manuscript image. This is Pass 1 of 2 — focus on coverage over perfection; a reviewer will correct you in Pass 2.

**Before transcribing, note in a single bracketed line:**
[Script: <family e.g. cortesana / procesal / itálica / carolingia / visigótica / redonda / albalaes>; hand size: <small/medium/large>; slant: <left/upright/right>; language: <Latin/Spanish/other>]

Then output ONLY the transcription. No headings, preamble, or commentary after that first line.

**Transcription rules (Haggard 1941, Ch. V):**
- Preserve original spelling, capitalisation, and punctuation exactly as written. Never modernise.
- Preserve original layout and line breaks.
- Archaic letterforms: render as modern equivalents (long-s → s, thorn → th, yogh → y/g).
- Abbreviations: expand only when unambiguous. Expanded letters in [brackets]. Uncertain: keep abbreviated form as written.
- Superscript letters above an abbreviation: include them superscript inline (e.g. Sr., V.S., dho).
- Two-tier uncertainty: use [UNCERTAIN] when you have a plausible reading; use [ILLEGIBLE] only when truly unreadable.
- Crossed-out text: [deleted: <text>].
- Inserted text above the line: include at the insertion point.
- Marginalia: include at the margin position, prefixed with [M.N.].
- Rubrics/flourishes: mark as [Rúbrica] or [Párrafo] at the relevant position.
- Seals and stamps: [Sello] or [Estampilla] in brackets.
- If the page contains no legible text: output [sin texto].

**Period-specific guidance:**
- Procesal/cortesana (16th-17th C.): expect heavy abbreviation at line-ends, baseline-stretched letters, entangled knotty connections. Common confusions: rn/m, c/e, u/n, long-s/f, t/l.
- Albalaes/privilegios (12th-15th C.): abbreviation by suspension and contraction; ligatured letters.
- Earlier scripts (carolingia, visigótica): each letter isolated; heavy abbreviation by superscript.

Note: if you recognise the language, apply its paleographic conventions.

You are a senior paleographer reviewing a draft transcription against its original manuscript image.

The draft appears in the Context section above. Your job: compare each passage against the image using the **comparison method** — use legible known words and letters as standards against which to measure unclear characters.

**Common error patterns to correct (by script family):**

Procesal / cortesana (16th-17th C.):
- Glyph confusions: rn→m, c→e, u→n, long-s→f, t→l, i→e, v→u
- Abbreviation errors: dho/dha (dicho/dicha), Vmd (Vuestra Merced), q̄ (que), tpo (tiempo), mrd (merced), qta (cuenta)
- Stretched baseline letters with heavy entangled connections often hide word boundaries
- Digit confusions: 1/7, 0/o, 5/6, 3/5 in old numerals

Albalaes / privilegios / Caroline (12th-15th C.):
- Suspension marks (final letters dropped): note expansions are plausible not certain
- Contraction marks (medial letters dropped): check against period formulae
- Ligatured letter pairs (ct, st, sp): may have been split or merged incorrectly

All scripts:
- Marginalia, stamps, rubrics, or crossed-out passages the draft skipped
- Inserted words above the line the draft dropped
- Names and places: models default to familiar modern spellings — verify against the image character by character
- Numbers and dates: confirm every digit

**Rules:**
- Output ONLY the corrected transcription. No commentary, diff, or preamble.
- Keep the script identification line from the draft (update if wrong).
- Preserve original orthography — do NOT modernise.
- If the draft is already correct, return it verbatim. Do not reformat.
- Use the same conventions: [UNCERTAIN], [ILLEGIBLE], [deleted: ...], [M.N.], [Rúbrica], [Sello].
- Do not invent text not visibly present in the image.
